source.original_text: For every fixed orthogonal tuple in the source block precision family, the actual centered Gaussian target becomes the independent product of its actual block Gaussians and the residual standard Gaussian under the literal contiguous coordinate split. This is the ASTIS-completed conditional ingredient of the printed prior-averaged Eq6. \mathrm{split}_{\#}\mathcal N(0,A_{\boldsymbol O}^{-1})=\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{k}\mathcal N(0,A_{O_j}^{-1})\right)\otimes\mathcal N(0,I_r). \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), with inclusive endpoints. Put \(k=\lfloor d/n\rfloor\) and \(r=d-kn=d\bmod n\). \(\boldsymbol O=(O_1,\ldots,O_k)\in O(n)^k\) is any fixed tuple in the full real orthogonal group. The matrices may differ and their determinant signs may differ; no prior on the tuple is supplied. \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\) and \(A_{\boldsymbol O}=\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r)\) are the existing literal source precision matrices. Positive definiteness, valid inverse covariances and independence are internal proof outputs. Coordinates are consecutive blocks: in zero-based indices, block entry \((j,i)\) is ambient coordinate \(jn+i\), and residual entry \(t\) is \(kn+t\). The split is a continuous linear coordinate bijection; no isometry for the ordinary max-normed product is asserted. When \(r=0\), the residual standard Gaussian is the unique probability measure on the zero-dimensional space. It is a point mass, not zero measure or a discarded unproved case. \mathrm{split}(x)=(x_1,\ldots,x_k,z),\quad (x_j)_i=x_{jn+i},\quad z_t=x_{kn+t}.

∀ {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (O : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →
        (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) :=
      fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
        WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
    (multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) ((Matrix.reindex e e (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => ((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))))) 0 0 (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ))))⁻¹).map split =
      (Measure.pi (fun j => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))))⁻¹)).prod
          (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))))
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin m) is real m-dimensional Euclidean space with its Borel structure; Fin m indexes coordinates from zero. WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp preserve coordinates. An ordinary finite function space and product carry their usual product Borel structures and default product norms.
Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) real is the full real orthogonal group with its usual matrix carrier, including both determinant signs.

Matrix.reindex e e M has entries M (e.symm i) (e.symm j). Matrix.blockDiagonal f uses index pairs (local coordinate, block index) and is zero between different blocks. Matrix.fromBlocks is the displayed two-by-two block assembly. finProdFinEquiv sends (a,b) to a times the cardinality of the second factor plus b; finSumFinEquiv concatenates its summands.

multivariateGaussian mean m covariance C is the pushforward of stdGaussian by z -> m + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (CFC.sqrt C) z. Its stated covariance interpretation holds for positive semidefinite C; outside that domain the constructor defaults to a point mass. Matrix inverse is totalized at singular matrices.

stdGaussian is the standard Gaussian obtained by independent scalar standard normal coordinates in an orthonormal basis. On a zero-dimensional Euclidean space it is the probability point mass at the sole vector.

Measure.map is the measurable pushforward operation. Measure.pi is the actual finite independent product of the displayed component measures, and Measure.prod is the actual binary product. Natural division and remainder and real scalar arithmetic have their usual Lean meanings.

reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers d and n with 3 ≤ n ≤ d, every real number κ with κ ≥ 4, and every family (O_j)_{j=0}^{q−1} of real n-by-n orthogonal matrices, where q = d div n and r = d mod n, define

A_j = ((κ + 1)/2) I_n − ((κ − 1)/4)(O_j + O_jᵀ).

Thus qn + r = d and 0 ≤ r < n. Order the d coordinates as q successive blocks of length n followed by r remaining coordinates. More precisely, let e be the bijection from ((Fin n × Fin q) ⊕ Fin r) to Fin d given by e(inl(i,j)) = jn + i and e(inr(k)) = qn + k. Let B be the d-by-d real matrix obtained by reindexing along e the block matrix with A_j on the jth n-dimensional diagonal block, identity I_r on the remainder block, and zero entries between different blocks. In these ordered coordinates B = diag(A_0, …, A_{q−1}, I_r).

Let S : R^d → ((Fin q → R^n) × R^r) be the coordinate splitting map
S(x) = ((x^{(j)})_{j∈Fin q}, x^{rem}),
where x^{(j)}_i = x_{jn+i} and x^{rem}_k = x_{qn+k}. Each R^m here is the real Euclidean space indexed by Fin m; the target has the ordinary finite-function and binary-product Borel structures.

The pushforward under S of the centered multivariate Gaussian constructed with covariance matrix B⁻¹ equals the finite independent product of the centered n-dimensional multivariate Gaussians constructed with covariance matrices A_j⁻¹, followed by an independent standard Gaussian on the r-dimensional remainder:

S_* multivariateGaussian(0, B⁻¹)
  = (⊗_{j∈Fin q} multivariateGaussian(0, A_j⁻¹)) ⊗ stdGaussian(R^r).

This is exact equality of measures on (Fin q → R^n) × R^r. Equivalently, if X has the measure on the left before splitting, its q block vectors have the displayed marginal Gaussian laws, the remainder vector is standard Gaussian, and all these block vectors and the remainder vector are mutually independent. Independence is asserted between these vectors; the coordinates inside an individual A_j⁻¹ block need not be independent.

The quantification is over every fixed orthogonal family, including matrices of either determinant sign; there is no averaging over orthogonal matrices. The only hypotheses supplied by the caller are 3 ≤ n, n ≤ d, and 4 ≤ κ, in addition to orthogonal-group membership. In particular, no positive-definiteness or invertibility hypothesis is separately required. Orthogonality and these scalar inequalities imply I_n ≤ A_j ≤ κ I_n in the quadratic-form order, so A_j and B are positive definite, and their inverse matrices are positive definite as well. Consequently the covariance terminology has its usual meaning for all parameters allowed here. Syntactically, however, the statement uses the approved totalized matrix inverse and Gaussian constructor: at singular matrices the inverse is totalized, and outside the positive-semidefinite domain the Gaussian constructor defaults to a point mass. Those conventions are part of the definitions, not additional caller hypotheses or an extension of this statement to parameters outside its stated range.

The endpoints n = 3, n = d, and κ = 4 are included whenever the other hypotheses hold. The hypotheses give q ≥ 1. The remainder r may equal zero; then R^0 consists of its sole zero vector, I_0 is the empty identity matrix, and stdGaussian(R^0) is the probability point mass there. The equality retains its binary remainder factor in this case. The coordinate splitting is understood as a measurable coordinate bijection; the statement does not require it to be an isometry for the default product norms.

There are no unspecified constants or asymptotic quantifiers. The block matrices depend only on κ and their respective O_j; q, r, e, S, and the assembled matrix B depend on the indicated d, n, κ, and orthogonal family through these explicit formulas. This reconstruction states the supplied proposition and its definition-level interpretation; it does not assert a proof of the proposition or correspondence to an unseen source.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.BlockFamily
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate

/-!
# The actual conditional block Gaussian law

Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1, Section 3.1 Eq4--Eq6 and the
regularity producer in Appendix B.3. This supplies the implicit fixed-tuple
Gaussian product-law ingredient. The source prints the prior-averaged Eq6;
its actual averaging, density, tensorization and amplification remain separate.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianBlockLaw
set_option autoImplicit false

theorem actual_conditional_block_product {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (O : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →
        (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) :=
      fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
        WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
    (multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (blockPrecision κ O)⁻¹).map split =
      (Measure.pi (fun j => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹)).prod
          (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)))) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let En := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
  let Er := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))
  let F := (Fin (d / n) → En) × Er
  let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
    ((Equiv.sumCongr
      ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
      (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
      (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
  let B := Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => singleBlockPrecision κ (O j)))
    0 0 (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)
  let C := Matrix.fromBlocks
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹))
    0 0 (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)
  have hp (j : Fin (d / n)) : (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j)).PosDef := by
    have hr := singleBlockPrecision_regular hn hκ (O j)
    apply Matrix.posDef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec.mpr
    refine ⟨hr.1, fun v hv => ?_⟩
    have hdot : 0 < v ⬝ᵥ v := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using (dotProduct_star_self_pos_iff.mpr hv)
    simpa only [star_trivial] using lt_of_lt_of_le hdot (hr.2 v).1
  have hBC : B * C = 1 := by
    dsimp only [B, C]
    rw [Matrix.fromBlocks_multiply, ← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
    simp only [Matrix.mul_zero, Matrix.zero_mul, add_zero, zero_add, Matrix.mul_one]
    have hmul : (fun j => singleBlockPrecision κ (O j) *
        (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹) = 1 := by
      funext j
      exact Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv _ ((Matrix.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det _).mp (hp j).isUnit)
    rw [hmul, Matrix.blockDiagonal_one]
    exact Matrix.fromBlocks_one
  have hAdef : blockPrecision κ O = Matrix.reindex e e B := rfl
  have hInv : (blockPrecision κ O)⁻¹ = Matrix.reindex e e C := by
    rw [hAdef, Matrix.inv_reindex, Matrix.inv_eq_right_inv hBC]
  have hpd : (blockPrecision κ O).PosDef := by
    have hr := blockPrecision_regular hn hnd hκ O
    apply Matrix.posDef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec.mpr
    refine ⟨hr.1, fun v hv => ?_⟩
    have hdot : 0 < v ⬝ᵥ v := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using (dotProduct_star_self_pos_iff.mpr hv)
    simpa only [star_trivial] using lt_of_lt_of_le hdot (hr.2 v).1
  let split : E → F := fun x =>
    (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
  let Tlin : E →ₗ[ℝ] F :=
    { toFun := split
      map_add' := by intro x y; ext i j <;> rfl
      map_smul' := by intro a x; ext i j <;> rfl }
  let T : E →L[ℝ] F := Tlin.toContinuousLinearMap
  let μ := multivariateGaussian (0 : E) (blockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
  let νj (j : Fin (d / n)) := multivariateGaussian (0 : En)
    (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹
  let νr := multivariateGaussian (0 : Er)
    (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)
  change μ.map split = (Measure.pi νj).prod (stdGaussian Er)
  rw [← multivariateGaussian_zero_one (ι := Fin (d % n))]
  change μ.map T = (Measure.pi νj).prod νr
  apply Measure.ext_of_charFunDual
  funext L
  rw [charFunDual_map, charFunDual_prod, charFunDual_pi]
  let Lb := L.comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inl ℝ (Fin (d / n) → En) Er)
  let Lj (j : Fin (d / n)) :=
    Lb.comp (ContinuousLinearMap.single ℝ (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => En) j)
  let Lr := L.comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (Fin (d / n) → En) Er)
  let vj (j : Fin (d / n)) : En := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ En).symm (Lj j)
  let vr : Er := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ Er).symm Lr
  let w : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) → ℝ :=
    Sum.elim (fun ij => vj ij.2 ij.1) (fun i => vr i)
  let v : E := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => w (e.symm i))
  have heval (i) : v (e i) = w i := by simp [v]
  have hinner (x : E) :
      ⟪v, x⟫ = (∑ j, ⟪vj j, (split x).1 j⟫) + ⟪vr, (split x).2⟫ := by
    change (∑ i : Fin d, x i * v i) =
      (∑ j, ∑ i : Fin n, (split x).1 j i * vj j i) +
        ∑ i : Fin (d % n), (split x).2 i * vr i
    rw [← e.sum_comp (fun i => x i * v i)]
    simp only [heval, Fintype.sum_sum_type, Fintype.sum_prod_type, w,
      Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr]
    dsimp only [split]
    congr 1
    exact Finset.sum_comm
  have hvfunctional : L.comp T = InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E v := by
    ext x
    change L (split x) = ⟪v, x⟫
    rw [hinner]
    simp_rw [vj, vr, InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply]
    rw [show (∑ j, (Lj j) ((split x).1 j)) = Lb (split x).1 from
      ContinuousLinearMap.sum_comp_single ℝ _ Lb (split x).1]
    exact (L.comp_inl_add_comp_inr (split x)).symm
  have hvec (z : Fin n × Fin (d / n) → ℝ) (i : Fin n) (j : Fin (d / n)) :
      (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹) *ᵥ z) (i, j) =
        ((singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹ *ᵥ (fun a => z (a, j))) i := by
    simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
      ite_mul]
  have hchange (M : Matrix ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n))
      ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ℝ) :
      WithLp.ofLp v ⬝ᵥ (Matrix.reindex e e M *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v) =
        (WithLp.ofLp v ∘ e) ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ (WithLp.ofLp v ∘ e)) := by
    change WithLp.ofLp v ⬝ᵥ (M.submatrix e.symm e.symm *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v) = _
    rw [Matrix.submatrix_mulVec_equiv]
    exact dotProduct_comp_equiv_symm _ _ e
  have hy : WithLp.ofLp v ∘ e = w := by
    funext i
    exact heval i
  have hquad : WithLp.ofLp v ⬝ᵥ ((blockPrecision κ O)⁻¹ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v) =
      (∑ j, WithLp.ofLp (vj j) ⬝ᵥ
        ((singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp (vj j))) +
          WithLp.ofLp vr ⬝ᵥ WithLp.ofLp vr := by
    rw [hInv, hchange, hy]
    simp only [C, Matrix.fromBlocks_mulVec, Matrix.zero_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec,
      add_zero, zero_add]
    rw [Matrix.dotProduct_block]
    congr 1
    simp only [dotProduct, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Function.comp_apply, w,
      Sum.elim_inl, hvec]
    exact Finset.sum_comm
  have hG {m : ℕ} (S : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ) (hS : S.PosSemidef)
      (K : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] ℝ) :
      charFunDual (multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) S) K =
        Complex.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ
          (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))).symm K) ⬝ᵥ (S *ᵥ
          WithLp.ofLp ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ
            (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))).symm K)) : ℝ) : ℂ) / 2) := by
    rw [← charFun_toDual_symm_eq_charFunDual, charFun_multivariateGaussian hS]
    simp [neg_div]
  have hw : (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm (L.comp T) = v := by
    rw [hvfunctional]
    exact (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm_apply_apply v
  have hb (j : Fin (d / n)) : charFunDual (νj j) (Lj j) =
      Complex.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp (vj j) ⬝ᵥ
        ((singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp (vj j)) : ℝ) : ℂ) / 2) :=
    hG _ (hp j).inv.posSemidef (Lj j)
  have hr : charFunDual νr Lr =
      Complex.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp vr ⬝ᵥ WithLp.ofLp vr : ℝ) : ℂ) / 2) := by
    simpa only [Matrix.one_mulVec] using
      hG (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ) Matrix.PosSemidef.one Lr
  change charFunDual μ (L.comp T) = (∏ j, charFunDual (νj j) (Lj j)) * charFunDual νr Lr
  rw [hG _ hpd.inv.posSemidef (L.comp T), hw, hr]
  simp_rw [hb]
  rw [← Complex.exp_sum, ← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  rw [hquad]
  push_cast
  simp only [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  ring

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianBlockLaw

steps.title: Produce admissible Gaussian covariances
steps.text: Apply the canonical single-block and ambient quadratic bounds. Their lower bounds imply strict positivity away from zero, hence invertibility and positive inverse covariance. This excludes the Gaussian constructor’s off-domain fallback internally.
steps.formula: I\preceq A_{O_j}\preceq\kappa I,\quad I\preceq A_{\boldsymbol O}\preceq\kappa I\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_{O_j},A_{\boldsymbol O}\succ0.
steps.lean: hp and hpd consume singleBlockPrecision_regular and blockPrecision_regular. Matrix.posDef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec, dotProduct_star_self_pos_iff and PosDef.inv supply the actual domain facts.

steps.title: Invert the literal block precision
steps.text: Multiply the unreindexed block matrix by the block diagonal matrix of actual inverses. Each block product is the identity, including the residual identity. Uniqueness of the inverse and exact reindexing identify the full covariance; the desired law is not defined to be a product. Here [M]_e denotes simultaneous row and column reindexing into the ambient contiguous coordinates.
steps.lean: hBC uses fromBlocks_multiply, blockDiagonal_mul and each genuine mul_nonsing_inv. hAdef is a definitional equality with the unchanged canonical precision; hInv uses inv_eq_right_inv and inv_reindex.

steps.title: Pull back every product-space frequency
steps.text: The explicit split is linear and continuous. Decompose an arbitrary continuous linear functional on the ordinary product into block and residual parts. Riesz representation in each Euclidean factor assembles one ambient frequency. Thus the argument tests every dual frequency without treating the max-normed product as Hilbert.
steps.lean: Tlin and T are the actual split. hinner and hvfunctional use the exact finite-coordinate equivalence, sum_comp_single, comp_inl_add_comp_inr and the real Euclidean Riesz map.

steps.title: Factor the actual Gaussian characteristic function
steps.text: The covariance quadratic form splits into the sum of block inverse-covariance forms and the residual square norm. The canonical Gaussian characteristic formula becomes a product of the block characteristic functions. All covariance validity conditions come from the first step.
steps.formula: v^\top A_{\boldsymbol O}^{-1}v=\sum_jv_j^\top A_{O_j}^{-1}v_j+\|v_r\|^2,\qquad e^{-v^\top A_{\boldsymbol O}^{-1}v/2}=\prod_j e^{-v_j^\top A_{O_j}^{-1}v_j/2}\,e^{-\|v_r\|^2/2}.
steps.lean: hchange and hquad transport the exact block covariance. hG is a local restatement of Mathlib.charFun_multivariateGaussian through the Riesz map; hb and hr specialize it. No independent characteristic-function equality is assumed.

steps.title: Identify measures and consume their true marginals
steps.text: Finite-product and binary-product characteristic functions give the same expression at every continuous dual functional. Uniqueness therefore gives the full measure equality. The focused consumer then pushes this same actual law to any block and to the residual, recovering their actual Gaussian laws. Separate checks establish the contiguous coordinates, inverse assembly and zero-dimensional probability point mass.
steps.lean: The proof uses charFunDual_map/prod/pi, Complex.exp_sum/add and Measure.ext_of_charFunDual. Tests.GaussianComplexityConditionalBlockLaw derives genuine block/residual marginal equalities with measurePreserving_eval and product projections; these are not a scalar substitute for the joint law.
